subject: General Science

questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Work done can only be negative.
Work done can be positive or negative depending on the direction of force.
Work done does not depend on force or displacement.
Work done can only be positive.
questions.explain: Work done is a scalar product of force and displacement ($W = F \cdot d \cos(\theta)$). Depending on the angle $\theta$ between the force and displacement vectors, the work done can be positive, negative, or zero.

questions.q: The power of a lens is defined as:
options: The reciprocal of its focal length in meters
The ratio of image distance to object distance
The product of its focal length and refractive index
The square of its focal length
questions.explain: The power of a lens is mathematically defined as the reciprocal of its focal length expressed in meters ($P = \frac{1}{f}$).
questions.subject: General Science

questions.q: When a thick glass slab is placed over printed matter, the letters appear raised. This is due to ___________.
questions.explain: When light travels from a denser medium (glass slab) to a rarer medium (air), it bends away from the normal. This bending of light is called refraction, which causes the letters to appear raised.
questions.subject: General Science

questions.q: The motion of a satellite orbiting the Earth in a circular path at constant speed is a classic example of uniform circular motion. What property of this motion prevents its acceleration from being zero?
options: The total mechanical energy is conserved, necessitating acceleration.
The direction of motion changes continuously at every point, meaning the velocity is changing.
The object's mass continually changes due to orbital dynamics.
The speed is too high for the gravitational force to sustain a constant velocity.
questions.explain: In uniform circular motion, although the speed is constant, the direction of motion continuously changes. Since velocity is a vector quantity, a change in direction means a change in velocity, thus yielding a non-zero centripetal acceleration.
questions.subject: General Science

questions.q: Which of the following describes an example of uniform circular motion?
options: A train moving on its track
A car accelerating on its way
A fan blade rotating at constant speed
questions.explain: A fan blade rotating at a constant speed travels in a circular path at a steady rate, perfectly describing uniform circular motion.
questions.subject: General Science

questions.q: A coil has a resistance of $44 \Omega$. If it is connected across a 220 V supply, what is the power consumed by the coil?
questions.explain: Power is given by the formula $P = \frac{V^2}{R}$. Substituting the values: $P = \frac{220^2}{44} = \frac{48400}{44} = 1100\text{ W}$.
questions.subject: General Science

questions.q: A body is dropped from a height. If it falls for 3.0 s and $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, its final velocity (v) is ____________.
questions.explain: Using the first equation of motion, $v = u + gt$. Because the object is dropped, initial velocity $u = 0$. So, $v = 0 + (10)(3.0) = 30\text{ m/s}$.

questions.q:
Statement 1: The potential difference is measured in volts.
Statement 2: One volt is equal to one newton per coulomb.
Which of the following is true?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct (potential difference is indeed measured in volts). Statement 2 is incorrect because one volt is defined as one joule per coulomb ($1\text{ V} = 1\text{ J/C}$), not one newton per coulomb.
questions.subject: General Science

questions.q: The frequency of a sound wave is 50 Hz. How much time will it take to complete one wave?
questions.explain: The time required to complete one wave is the time period ($T$). The relationship between time period and frequency ($f$) is $T = \frac{1}{f}$. Given $f = 50\text{ Hz}$, $T = \frac{1}{50} = 0.02\text{ s}$.
